source: Seven learning exchanges saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Purpose and reason recall, not yet versus now, testing vocabulary
summary: Recalled Leemos para aprender español and Leemos porque queremos aprender español, with spelling corrections only. Readiness recall initially confused object lo with subject it and ya with not yet. After correction, todavía placement was valid; feminine lista needed correction. Correctly transferred todavía no to ability, then switched to ya. Recalled Queremos probarla without a Spanish form hint.

observations.outcome: Correct leemos and para + infinitive without a form hint; capitalization and ñ supplied.
Correct reason clause and queremos recalled after intervening readiness practice. Supplied ñ; no verb correction needed.

Requested It isn't ready yet. Incorrect subject lo and use of ya for requested not yet corrected. Tutor explained todavía no and that subject it is unstated here; lo is an object pronoun. Masculine listo and negation otherwise appropriate.

observations.learnerText: Todavia la funcion no esta listo
observations.correctedText: Todavía la función no está lista.
observations.outcome: Valid initial todavía placement and subject la función after the model. Correct time meaning, but feminine lista needed correction. Tutor also modelled La función todavía no está lista. Accents supplied.
Correct transfer of todavía no to ability and feminine object la for stated function referent. Accent/capitalization supplied; immediate practice, not delayed retention.
Correct switch from not yet to now, using natural sentence-final ya and retaining la.

Correct queremos, probar and feminine object la for the stated función referent. No Spanish form or vocabulary hint provided; earlier version in session03 included a probar reminder. This remains same-day recall.

nextSteps: Recheck feminine readiness with todavía no after intervening material
Recheck omission of subject it and distinguish it from object lo/la
Review location with estar, which has not yet had an independent correct retry
Return to earlier goals and permission phrases before adding more grammar
assessmentNote: Correct immediate transfer after a model is distinguished from same-day recall without a form hint. No evidence of long-term retention. Orthography assessed separately; no keyboard limitation assumed.
